source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 11
statement: A policy document is read strictly (schema 2) by every version (RFC 0014 R4). A later version changes what an older reader decides only in a form the older reader refuses to compile (a member it does not know, a reserved character), never by giving another meaning to what the older reader already compiles; that is why the characters a later syntax needs are reserved from 8.0.0-beta.9 (DOC-15). A document either version compiles, the other compiles too; a pattern one version refuses, the other refuses too; an escape and a wildcard mean the same to both, decided through each version's engine. A DENY stored while 8.0.0-beta.8 ran, whose pattern holds a backslash beta.8 read as text, rewritten as the upgrade notes give (kept beside its exact form), denies in both versions what beta.8 denied.
guards: compat:DocumentCompatTest#a document either version compiles, the other compiles too
compat:DocumentCompatTest#a pattern one version reserves, the other refuses too
compat:DocumentCompatTest#an escaped DENY denies its path in both versions
compat:DocumentCompatTest#a wildcard matches alike in both versions, and one within a segment or a verb is refused by both
compat:DocumentCompatTest#an escape is the character to both versions
compat:DocumentCompatTest#a backslash DENY kept beside its exact form denies what was meant in both versions
